system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: =gptel-directives= | Alist of system directives, can switch on the fly.
system_prompt_style.note: System message is a selectable fixed directive string; presets can set :system.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: you can add a selected region, buffer or file to gptel's context from the menu, or call =gptel-add=
env_context_strategy.evidence_locator: README.org Include more context with requests
env_context_strategy.note: User-added live context is injected; tools (user-supplied) can allow navigation. Default: buffer text up to cursor only.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: By default, gptel will query the LLM with the active region or the buffer contents up to the cursor.
context_compaction.evidence_locator: README.org Include more context with requests
context_compaction.note: No condenser/summarizer described; gptel-max-tokens caps query+response.

observation_format.note: Media is input, not tool observation; tool results are text returned to the LLM.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: If the LLM decides to run the tool, it supplies the tool call arguments, which gptel uses to run the tool in your Emacs session.

tool_count.evidence_quote: gptel does not currently include any tools out of the box.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: gptel does not currently include any tools out of the box.
edit_primitive.note: gptel-rewrite edits regions in-buffer with diff/merge, but no model-facing edit tool ships.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: the tool specification requires a =:name=, =:description= and a list of argument specifications in =:args=

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration using [[https://github.com/lizqwerscott/mcp.el][mcp.el]].

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The result is optionally returned to the LLM to complete the task.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: gptel's default usage pattern is simple, and will stay this way: Read input in any buffer and insert the response below it.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: gptel is a simple Large Language Model chat client for Emacs, with support for multiple models and backends.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: gptel is a simple Large Language Model chat client for Emacs, with support for multiple models and backends.

human_in_loop.note: Also: user edits/sends each prompt; dry-run lets you inspect and edit requests before sending.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: gptel uses [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/elisp/Text-Properties.html][text-properties]] to watermark LLM responses.
short_term_state.evidence_locator: README.org FAQ How does gptel distinguish
short_term_state.note: The buffer text is the conversation state.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Save chats as regular Markdown/Org/Text files and resume them later.
long_term_memory.note: Saved chat files are re-read across sessions; no vector store or skill library.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Saving the file will save the state of the conversation as well. To resume the chat, open the file and turn on =gptel-mode= before editing the buffer.
state_persistence.evidence_locator: README.org Save and restore your chat sessions
state_persistence.note: Also "Pause multi-stage requests at an intermediate stage and resume them later."

self_verification.evidence_quote: gptel does not currently include any tools out of the box.
self_verification.note: No harness-run tests, linters or judges; human reviews rewrites via diff/ediff.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Pressing =RET= or clicking in the rewritten region should give you a list of options: you can *iterate* on, *diff*, *ediff*, *merge* or *accept* the replacement.
retry_policy.evidence_locator: README.org Rewrite, refactor or fill in a region
retry_policy.note: Iteration is user-initiated, not an automatic retry policy.

rollback.evidence_quote: The result is previewed over the original text. By default, the buffer is not modified.
rollback.evidence_locator: README.org Rewrite, refactor or fill in a region
rollback.note: No git/snapshot rollback; Emacs undo is outside gptel.

termination_condition.note: A request ends when the model finishes responding (no further tool calls).

cost_controls.evidence_quote: =gptel-cache= | Cache prompts, system message or tools (Anthropic only)

timeouts.note: No gptel-level timeout option documented; curl args could set one.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: which gptel uses to run the tool in your Emacs session
execution_isolation.note: Tools are elisp functions run in-process in the user's Emacs.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: you can get the LLM to control your Emacs frame, create or modify files and directories
filesystem_access.note: Context file addition restricted by gptel-context-restrict-to-project-files, but tools are unrestricted.

network_policy.evidence_quote: =gptel-proxy= | Proxy server for requests, passed to curl via =--proxy=.

permission_model.evidence_quote: From here you can also require confirmation for all tool calls, and decide if tool call results should be included in the LLM response.
permission_model.note: Configurable via gptel-confirm-tool-calls; also gptel-pre-tool-call-functions can block.

tracing.evidence_locator: README.org Introspection (examine, debug or modify requests)

replayability.evidence_quote: You can also copy a Curl command corresponding to the request and invoke it from the shell.
replayability.evidence_locator: README.org Introspection (examine, debug or modify requests)
